We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 6 reactions, using templates in order: ['20810', '2895', '1914397', '1914398', '1914399', '74054'].

We have retrieved template 20810 and applied it to target, got precursors: a tuple of two SMILES: ('CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1', 'O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F').

So first reaction (retro) splits target into those two precursors.

Now we need to continue retrosynthesis for each precursor using next templates in order.

We need to apply template 2895 to appropriate precursor(s). Template 2895 appears to be a transformation that converts an aniline (NH2) attached to aromatic to nitro? Actually retro_smarts: [C:7]-[#8:6]-[c:5]1...>>O=[N+;H0;D3:1](-[O-])-[c:2]1... So forward is nitro to phenoxy? Wait retro: product side is nitro aromatic, reactant side is phenoxy? The retro template likely breaks a nitro group to an aniline? Actually mapping: In retro, left side is product? The retro_smarts_template is left side (product) -> right side (reactants). So product is [C:7]-O-aryl with NH2? Wait left side: [C:7]-[#8:6]-[c:5]1...-NH2. Right side: nitro aromatic plus something? Actually right side: O=[N+;H0;D3:1](-[O-])-[c:2]1... So product is phenoxy with NH2, reactants are nitro aromatic plus something? So applying this template to a molecule with phenoxy-? Our precursor from 20810 includes a phenoxy? The first precursor: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1. This contains a phenoxy (c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2...). It has an aniline (N) attached to aromatic. So template 2895 likely splits that into nitro aromatic and something else (maybe the carbamate). So apply template 2895 to that precursor.

Let's apply.
